proposed.sourceName: IFANCA — The Halal Gelatin Story (M. Munir Chaudry, Ph.D.)
proposed.paraphrase: IFANCA states that in commercial gelatin production all halal and non-halal bones are mixed together regardless of source, so cow bones are mixed with pig bones; gelatin appearing on a label without a stated halal source must therefore be avoided.

proposed.sourceName: Heliyon — Towards halal pharmaceutical: Exploring alternatives to animal-based ingredients (Herdiana et al.)
proposed.paraphrase: Peer-reviewed review noting the most common gelatin raw material is porcine, and that halal status depends on source — undisclosed-source gelatin cannot be assumed permissible without halal certification.

researcherNote: Unspecified-origin gelatin: IFANCA's own account explains why unlabeled gelatin defaults to mixed pig/cattle bone and must be avoided. Grade is non-halal (draft 4), so the origin-undeterminable rule does not block it. High-traffic → two independent sources present. APPROVED by owner 2026-06-27.
